title: Trace entity repr and trace_id: expose trace.trace_id as a property over info.trace_id and quote it in repr
answers: Why does trace.trace_id raise AttributeError when repr(trace) shows a trace_id?
How is repr(Trace) formatted, and why is the trace id quoted?
Where is the trace id stored on a Trace object and how do I read it directly?
What does repr print for a Trace whose info is None?
body:
Path: The Trace entity in mlflow/entities/trace.py wraps a TraceInfo (`info`) and TraceData (`data`); tracing APIs that return traces to users (get and search results, fluent tracing) pass through it. Chokepoints are mlflow/entities/trace.py:Trace.trace_id and mlflow/entities/trace.py:Trace.__repr__.
Rule: The authoritative id is `info.trace_id`. Trace must not store a second copy; it exposes a read-only `trace_id` property that delegates to `self.info.trace_id`. `Trace.__repr__` must only advertise attributes that exist, print the id with `!r` so it is quoted valid Python, and read it defensively via `getattr(self.info, "trace_id", None) if self.info else None` so a Trace with info=None still prints `Trace(trace_id=None)`. Do not add deprecated aliases such as request_id on Trace; the PR dropped one after review.
Symptom: Users who saw `Trace(trace_id=...)` in repr and wrote `trace.trace_id` got an AttributeError, because the repr advertised a top-level attribute that did not exist; the id also printed unquoted.
Constraints: Applies to the Trace entity. TraceInfo.trace_id remains the real field and is unchanged. Covered by tests/entities/test_trace.py:test_trace_repr_and_trace_id.
applies: Trace entity in mlflow/entities/trace.py; applies to code that reads a trace's id or prints a Trace object, not to TraceInfo itself.
says: Accessing the identifier property on a returned trace object causes an attribute error.
Printed trace representations display an unquoted identifier that cannot be copied as valid code.
Allow reading the trace identifier directly from trace query and search results.
Printing a trace object that lacks metadata displays empty identifier values safely.
search: In mlflow/entities/trace.py, the Trace entity exposes a read-only trace_id property delegating to self.info.trace_id and formats Trace.__repr__ with quoted identifiers using !r. The __repr__ implementation safely inspects info with getattr so missing metadata prints Trace(trace_id=None), while deprecated aliases like request_id are omitted. Applies to the Trace entity returned by get, search, and fluent tracing APIs rather than TraceInfo itself, resolving AttributeError when accessing trace_id.
